[[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] congressman [[Jim Banks]] was elected to his first term, defeating [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] psychologist Valerie McCray in the general election.{{cite news |title=Indiana U.S. Senate Election Results 2024: McCray vs. Banks |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2024/11/05/us/elections/results-indiana-us-senate.html |access-date=November 7, 2024 |work=The New York Times |date=November 5, 2024}} Banks succeeded Republican incumbent [[Mike Braun]], who opted instead to [[2024 Indiana gubernatorial election|run for governor]].{{cite news |last1=Wren |first1=Adam |title=Braun to run for Indiana governor, opening Senate seat in 2024 |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2022/11/30/braun-to-run-for-indiana-governor-opening-senate-seat-in-2024-00071339 |work=POLITICO |date=November 30, 2022 |language=en}} This was the first election for this seat in which there was no incumbent running since [[1958 United States Senate election in Indiana|1958]].{{efn|[[Richard Lugar]], the incumbent Senator at the time, ran for re-election to a seventh term in [[2012 United States Senate election in Indiana|2012]], but lost in the Republican primary to [[Richard Mourdock]].}} On election day, Republican Banks defeated Democrat Valerie McCray by a near 20-percentage-point margin, winning all but three counties.
